name: Reading the Board
blurb: Four short boards that teach the whole game.

levels.outro: That is the whole idea. A number counts its own color, and sometimes that only leaves one answer.

teach.say: Every square is one of three colors — Coral, Teal or Butter. Three squares here are still blank.
This square is Coral, and it carries a 3. That means exactly three of the eight squares touching it are Coral too — diagonals count.
None of its painted neighbours are Coral. And only three squares are left. So all three of them must be Coral.
Pick Coral below, then paint those three squares.

levels.outro: Crosses are only your notes — the game never checks them and never fills anything in for you. Cornering the answer is your job.

teach.say: A 0 is the most useful clue on the board.
This Coral 0 touches no Coral at all — so neither blank square can be Coral.
Do not just remember it, mark it. Double-tap the 0 and it crosses Coral off every empty square it touches.
This Teal 0 says the same thing about Teal. Double-tap it too.
Both squares have Coral and Teal crossed off now. Only Butter is left — so paint them in.

levels.outro: Crossing out is not a hint — it is how you get there. Rule colors out and the answers appear.

teach.say: You can cross a color out by hand too. Switch to Cross below.
With Cross on, pick a color and tap a square to rule that color out there.
Rule two colors out of a square and the third one is your answer — then paint it in yourself. The 0 in the corner is the place to start.
Now finish the board. Tap the lightbulb if you get stuck — it always has a move you could have found.

levels.outro: You know the whole game now. Hearts come on from here — three wrong guesses and the board resets.

teach.say: One more. When a number is hard to read, tap it — the eight squares it watches light up.
A number fades once it has nothing left to tell you. The bright ones are the ones still worth reading.
